subject: math
cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skillName: Density in Area and Volume Models
intro: Eight multiple-choice questions on density as a quantity per unit area or per unit volume. Compute the relevant area or volume, then use $D = \frac{Q}{M}$, $Q = D \cdot M$, or $M = \frac{Q}{D}$, carrying units throughout.

items.prompt:
A rectangular county is $12$ mi by $8$ mi and has a population of $76{,}800$ people. What is its population density?
A) $800$ persons per $\text{mi}^2$
B) $0.00125$ persons per $\text{mi}^2$
C) $800$ persons per mile
D) $800$ (no units)

steps: Density is quantity divided by measure: $D = \frac{76{,}800}{96} = 800$ persons per $\text{mi}^2$.
A is correct. B divides in the wrong direction ($\frac{96}{76{,}800} = 0.00125$). C uses persons per mile, but area density is per square mile. D drops the compound unit entirely.

items.prompt:
A storage room is a rectangular prism $20$ ft by $15$ ft by $10$ ft, and a furnace must supply $90{,}000$ BTU to heat it. What is the heating requirement per cubic foot?
A) $30$ BTU per $\text{ft}^3$
B) $300$ BTU per $\text{ft}^2$
C) $300$ BTU per $\text{ft}^3$
D) $90{,}000$ BTU per $\text{ft}^3$

steps: Heating fills a space, so use volume: $V = 20 \cdot 15 \cdot 10 = 3000\text{ ft}^3$.
A is correct. B and C divide by a face area $20 \cdot 15 = 300\text{ ft}^2$ instead of the volume, mislabeling the unit too. D forgets to divide by the measure at all.

items.prompt:
A triangular plot has base $40$ m and height $30$ m and is planted with $1{,}200$ seedlings. What is the planting density?
A) $2$ seedlings per $\text{m}^2$
B) $1$ seedling per $\text{m}^2$
C) $0.5$ seedling per $\text{m}^2$
D) $40$ seedlings per $\text{m}^2$

steps: A is correct. B forgets the factor $\frac{1}{2}$ and divides by $40 \cdot 30 = 1200$. C compounds the missing $\frac{1}{2}$ further. D divides $\frac{1200}{30}$, using only one dimension.

items.prompt:
A circular irrigated field has radius $50$ m and is planted at $4$ corn plants per square meter. How many plants are there?
A) $10{,}000\pi$ plants
B) $200\pi$ plants
C) $625\pi$ plants
D) $2500\pi$ plants

steps: Area of the field: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi(50)^2 = 2500\pi\text{ m}^2$.

A is correct. B uses $\pi r = 50\pi$ (forgetting to square the radius), giving $200\pi$. C divides instead of multiplying by the density. D is just the area, not multiplied by the $4$ plants per $\text{m}^2$.

items.prompt:
A town has $54{,}000$ residents and a population density of $1500$ persons per square mile. The town is a square. What is the length of one side?
A) $6$ mi
B) $36$ mi
C) $\sqrt{1500}$ mi
D) $1500$ mi

steps: A is correct. B reports the area $36$ as if it were the side, forgetting the square root. C takes the root of the density rather than the area. D multiplies $1500 \cdot 54{,}000$ logic gone wrong by treating density as the side.

items.prompt:
A cylindrical grain silo has radius $4$ ft and height $18$ ft and holds $90{,}000$ lb of grain. What is the grain density?
A) $\frac{625}{2\pi}$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$
B) $312.5$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$
C) $\frac{1250}{\pi}$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$
D) $288\pi$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$

steps: A is correct. B drops the $\pi$ from the volume, computing $\frac{90{,}000}{288} = 312.5$. C uses radius $4$ unsquared ($\pi r h = 72\pi$), giving $\frac{90{,}000}{72\pi} = \frac{1250}{\pi}$. D reports the volume itself, not the density.

items.prompt:
A conical sand pile has radius $3$ ft and height $9$ ft and weighs $5400$ lb. What is its density?
A) $\frac{200}{\pi}$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$
B) $\frac{5400}{81\pi}$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$
C) $\frac{600}{\pi}$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$
D) $27\pi$ lb per $\text{ft}^3$

steps: A is correct. B forgets the $\frac{1}{3}$ factor and divides by $81\pi$ (the cylinder volume), underreporting the density. C miscomputes $\frac{5400}{9\pi}$. D reports the volume rather than the density.

items.prompt:
A rectangular orchard is $1{,}320$ ft by $660$ ft and contains $3{,}000$ trees. Using $1\text{ acre} = 43{,}560\text{ ft}^2$, what is the planting density in trees per acre, rounded to the nearest whole tree?
A) $150$ trees per acre
B) $20$ trees per acre
C) $3{,}000$ trees per acre
D) $145{,}200$ trees per acre

steps: A is correct. B reports the acreage $20$ instead of the density. C divides by $1$ as if the area were one acre. D divides $3000$ by the area in square feet wrong-way, or multiplies improperly, giving an unreasonable rate.
